newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain stocks tick up in buoyant trade.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain stocks tick up in buoyant trade.

text.p: Bahraini stocks ticked up in the week to Thursday in buoyant trade led by commercial banks, the Bahrain Stock Exchange said.
It said the index rose to 1,579.89 points from 1,571.09 points the previous week.

Around 12.4 million shares worth 2.7 million dinars ($7.2 million) changed hands, up from 6.6 million shares worth 1.37 million dinars last week. Last week's trade was shortened to four days due to the Eid al-Adha holiday.
Shares of 21 of the 39 firms registered in the exchange were traded in 354 transactions.
Activity focused on commercial banks, with stocks worth 1.04 million dinars traded. Commercial banks accounted for 63 percent of trade.
Al-Ahli Commercial Bank was the week's most active stock with shares worth 571,077 dinars traded. The stock closed at 344 fils, up from the previous week's 338 fils.
Bahrain Middle East Bank rose to 99 fils from 98 a week earlier.

Bahrain's bourse is open to nationals of the six Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Oman and Kuwait. Some firms are also open to foreign investors. ($1=0.377 dinar)
